title: नेपाली उपन्यासमा मानसिक विक्षिप्तता
nepali: नेपाली उपन्यासका विक्षिप्त पात्रहरूको मानसिक अवस्था र तिनको सामाजिक–आर्थिक अवस्थाबिचको अन्तःसम्बन्धको अध्ययन यस शोधकार्यमा गरिएको छ । व्यक्तिको आर्थिक, सामाजिक एवम् लैब्गिक विभेदले पात्रको मानसिक सन्तुलनमा प्रभाव पार्दछ । यसै सन्दर्भमा नेपाली उपन्यासका पात्रहरूको सामाजिक वर्ग र तिनको मानसिक समस्याबिच केकस्तो अन्तःसम्बन्ध रहेको छ भन्ने मूल समस्यामा केन्द्रित भएर यो अध्ययन गरिएको छ । यसको समाधानका लागि गरिबीका विरुद्ध प्रेम, आशब्का र पश्चात्तापले व्यक्तिको मानसिकतामा पारेको असर, सम्पन्नताविरुद्ध दमन, असमानता र विभेदले व्यक्तिको मानसिक सन्तुलनमा पारेको प्रभाव र बौद्धिकताका विरुद्ध विकृत राजनीतिक परिवेशले आममानिसको मानसिक स्वास्थ्यमा पारेको असर उपशीर्षकहरूमा नेपाली उपन्यासका पात्रहरूको अध्ययन गरिएको छ । यसका लागि सिग्मन्ड फ्रायडको मनोविश्लेषण सिद्धान्तका आधारमा विक्षिप्त पात्रहरूको खोजी गरी तिनको सामाजिक, आर्थिक अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यसरी गरिएको अध्ययनबाट गरिबी, अभाव र विपन्नताकै कारणले मात्र मान्छेको मानसिक सन्तुलन नबिग्रने, यसमा आशब्का र पश्चात्तापजन्य मनोभावको विकृतिले विक्षिप्तताको अवस्थासम्म पर्‍याउँछ भन्ने कुरा नेपाली उपन्यासमा व्यक्त गरिएको छ । यसका साथै निम्न वर्ग र निरक्षर व्यक्तिमाभन्दा उच्च वर्ग र साक्षर व्यक्तिमा मानसिक समस्या धेरै देखिएको स्थिति पनि नेपाली उपन्यासको अध्ययनबाट प्रस्ट भएको छ । विकृति, विभेद र दमनविरुद्धको चेतना विकसित भए पनि उनीहरूले त्यसविरुद्ध प्रतिरोध गर्ने उपयुक्त मार्ग पहिल्याउन नसक्दा नेपाली उपन्यासका पात्रका मानसिक सन्तुलनमा समस्या देखिएको निष्कर्ष यस अध्ययनले स्थापित गरेको छ ।
american_english: In this research work, the study of the interrelationship between the mental state of the mentally disturbed characters of Nepali novels and their socio-economic condition has been carried out. A person's economic, social and gender discrimination affects the mental balance of the character. In this context, this study has been conducted focusing on the main problem of what kind of interrelationship exists between the social class of the characters of Nepali novels and their mental problems. For its solution, a study of the characters of Nepali novels has been carried out under subheadings: the effect of love, hope and repentance on a person's mentality against poverty; the effect of oppression, inequality and discrimination on a person's mental balance against affluence; and the effect of a distorted political environment on the mental health of common people against intellect. For this, the mentally disturbed characters have been sought out and their social and economic condition analyzed on the basis of Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic theory. From the study carried out in this way, it has been expressed in Nepali novels that a person's mental balance is not disturbed by poverty, deprivation and destitution alone, and that the distortion of hope- and repentance-born sentiments leads to a state of mental disturbance. In addition, the study of Nepali novels has also made clear the situation in which mental problems are seen more in upper-class and literate persons than in lower-class and illiterate persons. Although consciousness against distortion, discrimination and oppression has developed, this study has established the conclusion that problems are seen in the mental balance of the characters of Nepali novels because they could not find an appropriate path to resist it.

informal_english: This study looks at how the mental state of disturbed characters in Nepali novels ties in with their socio-economic situation. A person's economic, social and gender-based discrimination affects their mental balance. With that in mind, the study zeroes in on the main question of what kind of link exists between the social class of characters in Nepali novels and their mental problems. To work through that, characters in Nepali novels were studied under subheadings: the effect of love, hope and repentance on a person's mentality against poverty; the effect of oppression, inequality and discrimination on a person's mental balance against affluence; and the effect of a distorted political environment on the mental health of ordinary folks against intellect. For this, disturbed characters were tracked down and their social and economic condition analyzed on the basis of Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic theory. From this study, Nepali novels express that a person's mental balance isn't disturbed by poverty, deprivation and destitution alone, and that the distortion of hope- and repentance-born feelings leads to a state of mental disturbance. On top of that, the study of Nepali novels has also made clear that mental problems show up more in upper-class and literate persons than in lower-class and illiterate ones. Even though awareness against distortion, discrimination and oppression has developed, the characters couldn't find a suitable way to resist it, and so problems show up in their mental balance — that's the conclusion this study has established.
